questions.q: Let $a, b, c$ be in arithmetic progression. Let the centroid of the triangle with vertices  \left(a, c\right), \left(2, b\right)$ and  \left(a, b\right)$ be \left(\dfrac{10}{3}, \dfrac{7}{3}\right) .$If $\alpha, \beta$are the roots of the equation $ax^{2} + bx + 1 = 0,$ then the value of ${α}^{2} + {β}^{2} - \alpha\beta$is:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{a + 2 + a}{3} = \dfrac{10}{3}$

$a = 4$

and~$\dfrac{c + b + b}{3} = \dfrac{7}{3}$

$c + 2b = 7$

also~$2b = a + c$

$2b - a + 2b = 7$

$b = \dfrac{11}{4}$

now~$4x^{2} + \dfrac{11}{4}x + 1 = 0$

~

${α}^{2} + {β}^{2} - \alpha\beta = \left(\alpha + \beta\right)$2 - $3\alpha\beta

$= \left(\dfrac{- 11}{16}\right)2 - 3 \$left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)$

$= \dfrac{121}{256} - \dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{- 71}{256}$

$$

$\begin{aligned} & \frac{x}{a}+\frac{y}{b}=1 \\ & \frac{3}{a}+\frac{5}{b}=1 \Rightarrow b=\frac{5 a}{a-3}, a \gt 3\end{aligned}$
$A=\frac{1}{2} a b=\frac{1}{2} a \frac{5 a}{(a-3)}=\frac{5}{2} \cdot \frac{a^2}{a-3}\begin{aligned} & =\frac{5}{2}\left(\frac{\mathrm{a}^2-9+9}{\mathrm{a}-3}\right) \\ & =\frac{5}{2}\left(\mathrm{a}+3+\frac{9}{\mathrm{a}-3}\right) \\ & =\frac{5}{2}\left(\mathrm{a}-3+\frac{9}{\mathrm{a}-3}+6\right) \geq 30\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A point $P$ moves on the line $2x - 3y + 4 = 0 .$ If $Q  \left(1, 4\right)$ and $R  \left(3, - 2\right)$ are fixed points, then the locus of the centroid of $\Delta PQR$ is a line:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let, coordinate of centroid is $( h, k )$ and coordinate of point $P$ is $( \alpha, \beta )$

We know that the centroid of a triangle with vertices~\left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}\right), \left({x}_{2}, {y}_{2}\right)~and~\left({x}_{3}, {y}_{3}\right)~is~\left(\dfrac{{x}_{1} + {x}_{2} + {x}_{3}}{3}, \dfrac{{y}_{1} + {y}_{2} + {y}_{3}}{3}\right) .

Hence, in~$∆ PQR,$~we have~\dfrac{\alpha + 1 + 3}{3} =$h$ and \dfrac{\beta + 4 - 2}{3} =$k$

$⇒ $\alpha =$3h - 4,$\beta =$3k - 2$

Since $( $\alpha, \beta ) lies on the line $2x - 3y + 4 = 0$

Hence, $2\left($3h - 4\right) - 3 \left(3k - 2\right) + 4 = 0$

$⇒ 6h - 9k + 2 = 0$

For finding the locus replace~\left(h, k\right)$~by~ \left(x, y\right)$

Hence, the~locus of centroid is $6x - 9y + 2 = 0$ which has slope $= - 6\left(- 9\right) = \dfrac{2}{3}$~since the slope of a line~$ax + by + c = 0$~is~$- \dfrac{a}{b} .$

$

questions.solution: The centroid $G^{\prime \prime}(\alpha, \beta)$ of $\triangle P Q R$ be image of centroid of given triangle $P^{\prime} Q^{\prime} R^{\prime}$. Centroid of $\Delta P^{\prime} Q^{\prime} R^{\prime}= \left(\frac{1+3+2}{3}, \frac{3+1+4}{3}\right)=$G^{\prime} \left($2, $\frac{8}{3}\right). Image of $G \left(2, \frac{8}{3}\right)$, w.r.t. line $x+2 y=2$ is $(\alpha, \beta)$ Then $\frac{\alpha-2}{1}=\frac{\beta-\frac{8}{3}}{2}=\frac{-2\left(2+\frac{16}{3}-2\right)}{1+4}\therefore \quad \frac{\alpha-2}{1}=\frac{\beta-\frac{8}{3}}{2}=-\frac{32}{15}\therefore \quad \alpha=-\frac{2}{15}$ and $\beta=-\frac{8}{5}$ Then $15(\alpha-\beta)=15\left(-\frac{2}{15}+\frac{24}{15}\right)=22$

If the perpendicular from origin $\mathrm{O}$ to this line makes an angle of $\frac{\pi}{6}$ with positive direction of $y$-axis and the area of $\triangle \mathrm{OAB}$ is $\frac{98}{3} \sqrt{3}$, then $\mathrm{a}^2-\mathrm{b}^2$ is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$Plotting the diagram of the given data we get,

Equation of straight line

Here given& $OA = a \text{ and } OB = b$, so equation of line~$AB$ in intercept form will be~$\dfrac{x}{a} + \dfrac{y}{b} = 1 . . . . . . \left(1\right)$

And given perpendicular line of length~$p$ is making~\dfrac{π}{3}~angle with the~$x -$axis,

So, the equation of line in normal form will be

$xcos\left(\dfrac{π}{3}\right) ++ysin\$left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) =p$

$⇒ \dfrac{x}{2p} + \dfrac{y\sqrt{3}}{2p} =1$

So, on comparing with the equation~ \left($1\right)$~we get,

$a = 2p \text{ and } b = $\dfrac{2p}{3}

Now area of the triangle $OAB$~is~

\dfrac{1}{2} \timesa \timesb = \dfrac{98\sqrt{3}}{3}

$⇒ $\dfrac{1}{2} \times$2p $\times \dfrac{2p}{3} = \dfrac{98\sqrt{3}}{3}

$⇒ p^{2} = 49$

Therefore,

$a^{2} - b^{2} = 4p^{2} - $\dfrac{4p^{2}}{3} = \dfrac{8}{3}$p^{2}$

$⇒ a^{2} - b^{2} = $\dfrac{8}{3}\left($49\right) = $\dfrac{392}{3}

questions.q: A point& $P$ moves so that the sum of squares of its distances from the points  \left(1, 2\right)$ and  \left(- 2, 1\right)$ is $14$. Let $f\left(x, y\right) = 0$~be the locus of $P$, which intersects the $x$-axis at the points $A, B$~and the $y$-axis at the point $C, D$. Then the area of the quadrilateral $ACBD$& is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

A point& $P$ moves so that the sum of squares of its distances from the points \left(1, 2\right)$ and \left(- 2, 1\right)$ is $14$.~

So,~\left(x - 1\right)2 + \left(y - 2\right)2 + \left(x + 2\right)2 + \left(y - 1\right)2 = 14$

$⇒ x^{2} + y^{2} + x - 3y - 2 = 0$

Put~$x = 0$

$⇒ y^{2} - 3y - 2 = 0$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{3 \pm \sqrt{17}}{2}$

Put~$y = 0$

$⇒ x^{2} + x - 2 = 0$

\left(x + 2\right)\left(x - 1\right) = 0$

$∴ A\left(- 2, 0\right), B \left(1, 0\right), C \left($0, $\dfrac{3 + \sqrt{17}}{2}\right),D\left($0, $\dfrac{3 - \sqrt{17}}{2}\right)

Area formed by~$ACBD$~will be~$= $\dfrac{1}{2}\left|\begin{cases}-$2 & 0 \\ 0 & $\dfrac{3 + \sqrt{17}}{2}$\\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & $\dfrac{3 - \sqrt{17}}{2}$\\ - 2 & 0\end{cases}\right|$

$= $\dfrac{1}{2}\left|-$3 - $\sqrt{17} - \dfrac{3}{2} - \dfrac{17}{2} + \dfrac{3}{2} - \dfrac{17}{2} +$3 - $\sqrt{17}\right|

$= $\dfrac{1}{2} \times$3 $\times \sqrt{17} = \dfrac{3\sqrt{17}}{2} \text{ and } sq units.

$

questions.q: In a triangle, the sum of lengths of two sides is $\mathrm{x}$ and the product of the lengths of the same two sides is $y$. if $x^{2}-c^{2}=y,$ where $c$ is the length of the third side of the triangle, then the circumradius of the triangle is

questions.solution: Let two sides of triangle are $a$ and $b$. $\begin{aligned}$& a+b=x \\ & a b=y \\ & x^{2}-c^{2}=y \Rightarrow(a+b)^{2}-c^{2}=a b \\ \Rightarrow &(a+b-c)(a+b+c)=a b \\ \Rightarrow & 2(s-c)(2 s)=a b \\ \Rightarrow & 4 s(s-c)=a b \\ \Rightarrow & $\frac{s(s-c)}{a b}=\frac{1}{4}$\\ \Rightarrow & \cos ^{2} $\frac{c}{2}=\frac{1}{4}$\\ \Rightarrow & \cos c=-$\frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow$c=120^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \end{aligned} $\therefore$ Area of triangle is, $\Delta=\frac{1}{2} a b\left(\sin 120^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}\right)=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} a b\because \quad R=\frac{a b c}{4 \Delta}\because \quad \mathrm{R}=\frac{a b c}{\sqrt{3} a b}=\frac{c}{\sqrt{3}}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Using section formula

Co-ordinates of $A = \left(\dfrac{1 \times 5 + 2 \times 0}{1 + 2}, \dfrac{1 \times 0 + 2 \times 4}{1 + 2}\right) = \left(\dfrac{5}{3}, \dfrac{8}{3}\right)
Co-ordinates of $B = \left(\dfrac{2 \times 5 + 1 \times 0}{1 + 2}, \dfrac{2 \times 0 + 1 \times 4}{1 + 2}\right) = \left(\dfrac{10}{3}, \dfrac{4}{3}\right)
Slope of $OA = {m}_{1} = $\dfrac{\dfrac{8}{3} - 0}{\dfrac{5}{3} - 0} = \dfrac{8}{5}
Slope of $OB = {m}_{2} = $\dfrac{\dfrac{4}{3} - 0}{\dfrac{10}{3} - 0} = \dfrac{2}{5}

We know that, tan\theta = \left|\dfrac{{m}_{1} - {m}_{2}}{1 + {m}_{1}{m}_{2}}\right|

$⇒ $tan\theta = \dfrac{65}{1 + \dfrac{16}{25}}

$⇒ $tan\theta = \dfrac{30}{41}

questions.q: If $x^{2} - y^{2} + 2hxy + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0$ is the locus of a point, which moves such that it is always equidistant from the lines $x + 2y + 7 = 0$ and $2x - y + 8 = 0$, then the value of $g + c + h - f$ equals
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let $P ( x, y )$ be the point whose distance from $x + 2y + 7 = 0$ and $2x - y + 8 = 0$ is equal.

$⇒ \dfrac{x + 2y + 7}{5} = \pm \dfrac{2x - y + 8}{5}$

$⇒ x^{2} + 4y^{2} + 49 + 4xy + 28y + 14x = 4x^{2} + y^{2} + 64 - 4xy - 16y + 32x$

$⇒ - 3x^{2} + 3y^{2} - 15 + 8xy + 44y - 18x = 0$

$⇒ 3x^{2} - 3y^{2} - 8xy + 18x - 44y + 15 = 0$

$⇒ x^{2} - y^{2} - \dfrac{8}{3}xy + 6x - \dfrac{44}{3}y + 5 = 0$

Now, on comparing $x^{2} - y^{2} + 2hxy + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0$ with above equation we get,

$⇒ h = \dfrac{- 4}{3}, g = 3, f = - \dfrac{22}{3}, c = 5$

$⇒ g + c + h - f = 3 + 5 - \dfrac{4}{3} + \dfrac{22}{3}$

$⇒ g + c + h - f = 14$

Given~$∆ ABC$~is an equilateral triangle,

So,~$sin\left(B\right) = \dfrac{h}{AB}$

questions.q: Two sides of a parallelogram are along the lines& $4x + 5y = 0$ and $7x + 2y = 0 .$ If the equation of one of the diagonals of the parallelogram is $11x + 7y = 9,$& then other diagonal passes through the point:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Both the lines& $4x + 5y = 0, 7x + 2y = 0$ pass through origin.

$D$~is~the point~of intersection of $4x + 5y = 0 \text{ and } 11x + 7y = 9$

So upon solving we get the~coordinates of point $D = \left(\dfrac{5}{3}, - \dfrac{4}{3}\right)

Also, point $B$~is the point of intersection of $7x + 2y = 0 & 11x + 7y = 9$

So, coordinates of point $B = \left(- \dfrac{2}{3}, \dfrac{7}{3}\right)$

The diagonals of parallelogram bisect each other, so~the mid point of~$BD$~is

\left(\dfrac{\dfrac{5}{3} - \dfrac{2}{3}}{2}, \dfrac{\dfrac{- 4}{3} + \dfrac{7}{3}}{2}\right) = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}, \dfrac{1}{2}\right)

The equation of diagonal~$AC$~is

\left(y - 0\right) = $\dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2} - 0}{\dfrac{1}{2} - 0}\left($x - 0\right)$~i.e.,~$y = x$

Therefore, the diagonal $AC$~passes through \left(2, 2\right) .$

$

questions.q: If a $∆ ABC$ has vertices~$A \left(– 1, 7\right), B  \left($– 7, 1\right)$ and~$C  \left(5, – 5\right)$, then its orthocentre has coordinates:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Slope of line& $BC$~is~${m}_{BC} = \dfrac{6}{- 12} = - \dfrac{1}{2}$

Slope of line~$AD = \dfrac{1}{mBC} = 2$

$∴$~Equation of line~$AD$~is~$y - 7 = 2 \left(x + 1\right)$

$⇒ y = 2x + 9 . . . \left(1\right)$

Slope of line~$AC$~is~${m}_{AC} = \dfrac{12}{- 6} = -2$

Slope of line~$BE = \dfrac{1}{mAC} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$∴$~Equation of~$BE$~is~$y - 1 = \dfrac{1}{2} \left(x + 7\right)$

$⇒ y = $\dfrac{x}{2} + \dfrac{9}{2} . . . \left(2\right)$

Comparing equations~ \left(1\right) & \left(2\right)$, we get

$2x + 9 = \dfrac{x + 9}{2}$

$⇒ 4x + 18 = x + 9$

$⇒ 3x = - 9 ⇒ x = - 3$

$∴ y = 2x + 9 = 3$

Therefore, orthocentre has co-ordinates~ \left(-3, 3\right)$.

$

questions.q: The equations of the sides $AB, BC$~and $CA$~of a triangle $ABC$~are $2x + y = 0, x + py = 15a$~and $x - y = 3$~respectively. If its orthocentre is  \left(2, a\right)$, $- \dfrac{1}{2} < a < 2$, then $p$& is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given the equations of the sides $AB, BC$~and $CA$~of a triangle $ABC$~are $2x + y = 0, x + py = 15a$~and $x - y = 3$~respectively.

Now on solving equation $2x + y = 0, x + py = 15a$~and~$x - y = 3$~we get coordinates of~$A \left(1, - 2\right), B \left(\dfrac{15a}{1 - 2p}, \dfrac{- 30a}{1 - 2p}\right)~and~$C = \left(\dfrac{18p - 30}{p + 1}, \dfrac{15p - 33}{p + 1}\right)$

And let orthocentre~be~$H \left($2, a\right)$

Slope of $AH = \dfrac{a + 2}{1}$

Sloe of $BC = - \dfrac{1}{p}$

As~$AH ⊥ BC$,~so~$p = a + 2$

Now coordinate of $C = \left(\dfrac{18p - 30}{p + 1}, \dfrac{15p - 33}{p + 1}\right)$

So, slope of $HC$

$= \dfrac{\dfrac{15p - 33}{p + 1} - a}{\dfrac{18p - 30}{p + 1} - 2} = \dfrac{15p - 33 - \left(p - 2\right)\left(p + 1\right)}{18p - 30 - 2p - 2}$

$= \dfrac{16p - p^{2} - 31}{16p - 32}$

Now~$HC ⊥ AB$, so $\text{slope of}HC \times \text{slope o$o$of}AB\text{=-$1}

$⇒ \dfrac{16p - p^{2} - 31}{16p - 32} \times -2 = - 1$

$⇒ p^{2} - 8p + 15 = 0$

$⇒ p = 3or5$

But if $p = 5$~then $a = 3$~not acceptable as~$p = a + 2$

$∴ p = 3

$

questions.solution: For $B^{\prime} \quad \frac{x-7}{2}=\frac{y-2}{1}=-2\left(\frac{14+2-6}{5}\right)\begin{aligned} & \frac{x-7}{2}=\frac{y-2}{1}=-4 \\ & x=-1 \quad y=-2 \quad B^{\prime}(-1,-2)\end{aligned}$ incident ray $\mathrm{AB}^{\prime}\begin{aligned} & M_{\mathrm{AB}^{\prime}}=3 \\ & y+2=3(x+1) \\ & 3 x-y+1=0 \\ & a=3 b=-1 \\ & a^2+b^2+3 a b=9+1-9=1\end{aligned}$
